text.p: The following are the main stories from Thursday's Albanian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Tirana was sealed off by hundreds of riot police on Wednesday, preventing opposition suporters and destitute investors from staging peaceful protests.
- President Sali Berisha cracks down on his adversaries within his ruling Democratic Party who had called on Prime Minister Aleksander Meksi to resign.
- Berisha, nearing the end of his first term in office, is not interested in changing the government, the paper says.

- Trade unions, political parties and several independent groups back Vlore residents who have staged more than a week of protests against the government's handling of the collapse of a series of pyramid investment schemes.
- Students and pupils in Tirana chanted "Vlore, Vlore" on Wednesday to express their solidarity with Vlore protesters.

- The paper's editorial attacks the Democratic Party, saying three dead, hundreds of injured and an estimated $2 billion tied up in dubious pyramid schemes should be enough to prompt the government's resignation.
- Prime Minister Meksi rejects calls for the government's dismissal or a cabinet reshuffle.
- A policeman, identified as Shezai Zani, was shot dead late on Wednesday in Vlore, the Interior Ministry said in a statement.

- Albania's exiled King Leka Zogu, who aspires to reinstate the monarchy founded by his father King Zog in 1928, said at his home in Johannesburg he expected Meksi to resign and vowed he was ready to step in.
- Thousands of protesters in Fieri, some 110 km (70 miles) south of Tirana, threatened to stage a march on the capital.
- The main opposition Forum for Democracy alliance renewed its call on all Albanians to hold rallies and protests every day at mid-day.

- Key opposition Socialist Party urges Berisha to release Sabit Brokaj, one of its leading members detained by police for allegedly inciting Vlore protesters to take up arms and topple the government.
- The paper publishes a petition of Vlore protesters calling on the government to resign and Berisha not to ask for a second term.

- Democratic Party leader Tritan Shehu rejects the idea of forming a multi-party coalition government and is quoted as saying his party would never accept a coalition with "red terrorists". terrorists".
